data.name: Baageshwari
data.gender_notes: Baageshwari is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Baageshwari is a name of the goddess Parvati, who is also known as Kamadhenu or the 'Goddess of Cows'. She is the source of all wealth and nourishment, and is often depicted as a beautiful woman holding a cow or a pot of ghee. This name signifies abundance, prosperity, and the blessing of the divine mother. The name Baageshwari carries the meaning “Goddess of Cows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Baageshwari usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of cows and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine feminine and the nurturing mother.
data.etymology: Baageshwari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Cows.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baageshwari total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

Temples and shrines dedicated to Baageshwari are popular pilgrimage sites, and devotees often offer milk, sweets, and other offerings to the goddess in the hope of receiving her blessings for prosperity and good fortune.

She is the embodiment of compassion and mercy, and is believed to be the giver of all material and spiritual blessings. Devotion to Baageshwari is said to bring peace, harmony, and contentment in one's life, and to help one overcome challenges and difficulties. Historical references suggest that the goddess was worshipped since ancient times, and her cult continued to flourish throughout the medieval period.

She is worshipped in various forms like Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kali, and Matangini.
